diagnostics.message: aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up must wait for aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up, which grants its execution role SQS polling permissions. Referencing the Lambda function alone does not order policy creation, so mapping creation can fail with insufficient ReceiveMessage permissions.
aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for scale_up_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured: Lambda needs the attached ENI permissions during creation, not merely an existing IAM role.
aws_lambda_function.scale_down must wait for scale_down_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured so its execution role has ENI permissions at creation.
aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for pool_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured; its role reference does not ensure the ENI permissions attachment exists.
aws_lambda_function.webhook must wait for webhook_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured so Lambda can create its network interfaces.
aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for syncer_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured so its execution role has ENI permissions during provisioning.

aws_s3_object.trigger immediately invokes the syncer through S3 notifications, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. Order the trigger after this policy so the initial invocation can write the runner distribution to S3.

aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms when a customer KMS key is configured; otherwise its immediate syncer invocation can run before the role can use the key to upload the distribution.
